teaching_blocks.title: The situation
teaching_blocks.content: A protected order endpoint needs tests of distinct denial gates as well as full success. One rejected request does not prove every security boundary works.

teaching_blocks.title: The rule and its boundary
teaching_blocks.content: Send requests through the real protected HTTP endpoint with absent, malformed and supplied bearer credentials, keeping the authentication and verification gates active.

teaching_blocks.title: How to use the rule
teaching_blocks.content: Test invalid-signature, expired and contextually wrong tokens separately from a valid token, asserting credential rejection before protected output is returned. Test an otherwise valid credential lacking the required permission separately from a valid sufficiently permitted credential to distinguish authentication from operation authorization. Test a valid caller against another caller's object identifier as a separate deny path from missing operation permission. Assert the declared status and safe body for each denial and the public projected result for the fully authorized request, not merely that some requests fail and one succeeds.

teaching_blocks.title: Reason through an example
teaching_blocks.content: Exercise the real endpoint with absent, malformed and supplied bearer credentials while keeping extraction and verification active. Separate invalid signature, expiry and wrong token context from a valid credential. Next use a valid credential lacking operation permission, then a valid caller requesting another caller's object. These isolate authentication, operation authorization and object authorization. Finally send a fully authorized request and assert the public projected result. For every denial, assert declared status and safe body before protected output is returned. Label each test by the gate it proves, not merely "fails." Substituting away verification would weaken the evidence precisely where this exercise requires real rejection behavior.

teaching_blocks.title: Keep this distinction
teaching_blocks.content: One denial plus one success is not complete security coverage. Isolate each credential and authorization failure while real gates remain active.

visual_anchor.purpose: Make the order-endpoint test matrix visible: credential condition, operation permission, requested order ownership, expected rejection gate, declared status and expected safe body or public result.

practice_anchor.objective: Test one protected order endpoint through real HTTP requests with absent, malformed, invalid-signature, expired, wrong-context, insufficient-permission and fully authorized credentials. Include a separately tested request for another caller's order.
practice_anchor.success: Each credential rejection, missing-permission denial and cross-object denial has its own test asserting the declared status and safe body without protected output. The fully authorized request returns the expected public projection, with authentication and verification active throughout.

live_code.required_skill: Write endpoint integration tests that isolate authentication, operation authorization and object authorization while checking complete response contracts.
allowed_syntax: headers dictionaries with Authorization bearer values
string literals and formatted resource paths
live_code.starter_state_intent: Provide a protected order endpoint, isolated orders belonging to two callers, the declared denial contracts and expected public order projection. Supply controlled bearer fixtures for invalid signature, expiry, wrong issuer or audience, missing operation permission and sufficient permission. Keep extraction, verification and both authorization gates active; leave the request cases and assertions for the learner.
live_code.observable_success: Tests send requests to the protected order endpoint rather than calling security helpers directly. Separate cases demonstrate credential rejection, permission denial, cross-object denial and authorized success, asserting exact declared statuses and safe denial bodies or the expected public order result.
